decisions.choice: the angel of the LORD: a messenger from the LORD who speaks with the LORD's own voice
decisions.reason: The word translated "angel" means "messenger", one sent with a message. This messenger does not say "the LORD says"; he speaks as God himself: "I brought you up ... my covenant". In other passages the angel of the LORD is both distinguished from the LORD and spoken of as the LORD (Genesis 16:7-13; Exodus 3:2-6; Judges 6:11-23; 13:21-22). So he may be a heavenly messenger who speaks for God so fully that his words are God's words, or an appearance of the LORD himself. The text does not settle which. The word can also mean a human messenger such as a prophet (compare 6:8), but the title "the angel of the LORD" in Judges always marks a heavenly visitor (6:11-22; 13:3-21).

decisions.choice: from Gilgal to Bochim: from Israel's first camp in the land to a place named for weeping
decisions.reason: Gilgal, near Jericho, was where Israel first camped after crossing the Jordan and where the covenant was renewed by circumcision and the Passover (Joshua 4:19; 5:2-10). The messenger comes from there, as if from the place of the first promises. Bochim means "weepers"; the place gets its name from what happens in verses 4-5. Where it lay is not known.

decisions.choice: the speech begins at once with "I brought you up"
alternatives: "This is what the LORD says: I brought you up"
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew text the messenger begins with God's words, with no "This is what the LORD says". The ancient Greek translation adds such an opening and also names Bethel beside Bochim. The Hebrew text is followed here; the shorter text fits the way the messenger speaks as God throughout.

decisions.choice: I will not break my covenant with you forever: God's promise to stay faithful
decisions.reason: God had promised that he would never break his covenant with Israel, even when he punished them (Leviticus 26:44; Deuteronomy 7:9). The promise is the background to the charge that follows: God has kept his side, Israel has not kept theirs (verse 2).

decisions.choice: promised on oath / promised with an oath
decisions.reason: The verb is "swore". Balanced and Readable say what the oath was, a promise God bound himself to keep.

decisions.choice: the deity_pronoun setting only on free pronouns and possessives ("agano langu|Langu")
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb ("niliwapandisha", "hamkunitii"), and a verb prefix cannot take a capital, so the capitalised-pronoun setting applies only to separate words such as possessives, "mimi", "nami" and "yeye". Where the English has a span on "me", the Swahili verb carries it and has none.

decisions.choice: "el ángel del SEÑOR" at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole of Judges, as the terms note for these books sets: the Hebrew word means a messenger, and here the messenger speaks with the LORD's own voice (m1). Spanish keeps the traditional "ángel" at every level, with the divine name setting on "del SEÑOR".

decisions.choice: the plural "you" in the "ustedes" form by default ("los", "les", "sus"), with the "vosotros" form ("os", "vuestros") under the plural-you setting; "padres" (L), "antepasados" (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Judges, as in the Pentateuch: wherever several people are addressed, the "ustedes" form of Latin America is the default and the plural-you setting gives the "vosotros" form of Spain, on pronouns, possessives and verbs. "Padres" and "antepasados" already take in both men and women, so they carry no gender span.

decisions.choice: "l'ange du SEIGNEUR" at every level
decisions.reason: For Judges 1-10, as the terms note sets: the Hebrew word means "messenger", and the meaning decision explains that this messenger speaks with the LORD's own voice. "L'ange" is the word French readers know for a messenger from God, and it is kept at every level as the English keeps "angel".

decisions.choice: deity pronoun setting on "mon" (my covenant), as on the English "my"
decisions.reason: For Judges 1-10: where God speaks of himself, French puts the deity pronoun setting on the possessive and object pronouns ("mon alliance", "ma voix", "m'obéir"), as the English does on "my" and "me"; "je" takes none, as the French style guide says.

decisions.choice: "thiên sứ của CHÚA"
decisions.reason: The terms note's form for the angel of the LORD. He speaks with the LORD's own voice (m1), so he says "Ta" as God does, with the deity_pronoun setting in the middle of a sentence.

decisions.choice: the LORD calls Israel "các ngươi"
decisions.reason: This is a rebuke to a people who have broken faith; "các ngươi" keeps the distance of a judge speaking, which "các con" would soften.

decisions.choice: "주의 천사" for the angel of the LORD, with no deity_pronoun spans in Korean
decisions.reason: "천사" with the divine name, as the terms of this translation set for Judges. The English marks pronouns for God with a capital-letter setting; Korean has no capital letters, so it has nothing to change, and respect for God is carried by the honorific -시- and 께서 at every level. This holds for the whole block. The angel speaks with God's own voice in the plain style (해라체), as God does.

decisions.choice: "조상들" for "your fathers", with no gender setting
decisions.reason: "조상" already means the forebears of a people, men and women, so Korean has one word where English has two; this holds for the whole block.

decisions.choice: o anjo do SENHOR
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 2:4; 5:23; 6:11-22; 13:3-21): the title keeps the Portuguese of Genesis 16:7 and docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md, with the article inside the divine-name setting. The messenger speaks as God himself (m1), so the pronouns for God in his speech take the deity_pronoun setting, as in the English.

decisions.choice: vocês (God to Israel); Boquim
decisions.reason: For the whole book: God, or his messenger, speaks to Israel in the plural with "vocês", as in Joshua and docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4. "Boquim" is the Brazilian form of the name (m2).

decisions.choice: no covenant with the inhabitants, tear down their altars: the commands of Exodus and Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: God had told Israel not to make a covenant with the peoples of Canaan and to break down their altars (Exodus 23:32-33; 34:12-13; Deuteronomy 7:2-5; 12:3). Chapter 1 has just shown tribe after tribe living alongside the Canaanites instead of driving them out (1:27-36).

decisions.choice: God's earlier words, quoted from verse 1, end with "pull down their altars"
alternatives: the quotation ends after "forever" in verse 1
decisions.reason: Verse 1 quotes what God said in the past, "I said ...". The quotation includes the two commands of this verse, and then the messenger turns to the present: "But you have not listened." The Hebrew has no quotation marks, so where the earlier words end is a matter of sense.

decisions.choice: listened to my voice: obeyed
decisions.reason: To "listen to the voice" of someone is to do what they say (Exodus 19:5; Deuteronomy 13:5). The charge is disobedience, not failure to hear.

decisions.choice: What is this you have done? A reproach, not a request for information
decisions.reason: The question is the same kind God asks Eve in Genesis 3:13: it confronts the hearers with what they have done.

decisions.choice: treaty

fr.R: Alors maintenant, je vous le dis : je ne les chasserai pas de votre chemin. Ils seront comme des épines plantées dans vos flancs, et leurs dieux seront un piège qui vous attrapera. »

vi.L: Và Ta cũng phán: Ta sẽ không đuổi chúng khỏi trước mặt các ngươi, và chúng sẽ [như gai nhọn đâm vào] hông các ngươi, và các thần của chúng sẽ là cạm bẫy cho các ngươi."
vi.B: Vậy nay Ta tuyên bố: Ta sẽ không đuổi chúng đi khỏi trước mặt các ngươi. Chúng sẽ thành gai nhọn đâm vào hông các ngươi, và các thần của chúng sẽ thành cạm bẫy cho các ngươi."
vi.R: Vì vậy, bây giờ Ta nói cho các ngươi biết: Ta sẽ không đuổi chúng đi cho các ngươi nữa. Chúng sẽ như gai nhọn đâm vào hông các ngươi, và các thần của chúng sẽ là cái bẫy bắt lấy các ngươi."

ko.L: 그러므로 나도 말한다. 내가 그들을 너희 앞에서 쫓아내지 않겠다. 그들이 너희 옆구리에 [가시가] 될 것이고, 그들의 신들이 너희에게 올무가 될 것이다."

ko.R: 그래서 이제 내가 너희에게 말한다. 나는 그들을 너희 앞에서 쫓아내지 않겠다. 그들은 너희 옆구리를 찌르는 가시처럼 될 것이다. 그리고 그들의 신들은 너희를 붙잡는 덫이 될 것이다."

pt.L: E também digo: Não os expulsarei de diante de vocês, e eles serão [espinhos nos] lados de vocês, e os deuses deles serão uma armadilha para vocês."
pt.B: Por isso agora declaro: Não os expulsarei de diante de vocês. Eles se tornarão espinhos nas costelas de vocês, e os deuses deles, uma armadilha para vocês."
pt.R: Por isso agora estou dizendo a vocês: Não vou tirar esses povos do caminho de vocês. Eles vão machucar vocês como espinhos na carne, e os deuses deles vão ser uma armadilha que vai prender vocês."

decisions.choice: I also say: God's declaration now, as a sentence on Israel
decisions.reason: The verb form usually tells of something past ("I said"), and it could point back to God's earlier warning that the nations would stay as thorns and traps if Israel disobeyed (Numbers 33:55; Joshua 23:13). But a verb of speaking in this form can also make a declaration at the moment of speaking ("I hereby say"). Here it follows the charge of verse 2 and the people weep at it (verse 4), so it is taken as the sentence God now pronounces. Both readings give the same outcome: the nations will stay.

decisions.choice: [thorns in] your sides: a constant pain and trouble
alternatives: they will be adversaries to you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they will be to you sides". Numbers 33:55 has the full picture: "thorns in your sides", and Joshua 23:13 has "thorns in your eyes". The short phrase is taken as pointing to that saying. Some read a word that differs by one letter, "adversaries" or "oppressors", which gives the same sense in plain words.

decisions.choice: their gods will be a snare: worship that will trap you
decisions.reason: A snare is a hunter's trap. God had warned that the gods of Canaan would trap Israel into serving them (Exodus 23:33; 34:12; Deuteronomy 7:16). Verses 11-13 tell how it happened.

decisions.choice: thorns in your sides
decisions.reason: The word "thorns" is supplied from Numbers 33:55 (see m2); Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: [espinhos nos] lados (L); espinhos nas costelas (B); como espinhos na carne (R)
decisions.reason: The picture is taken from Numbers 33:55 (m2), so each level keeps that verse's Portuguese: "espinhos nos seus lados" (L), "espinhos nas suas costelas" (B), and Readable's everyday "espinho na carne".

sw.R: Malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alipomaliza kuwaambia Waisraeli wote maneno hayo, watu walianza kulia na kuomboleza kwa sauti kubwa.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} habló estas palabras a todos los hijos de Israel, el pueblo alzó su voz y lloró.
es.B: En cuanto el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} terminó de decir estas palabras a todos los israelitas, el pueblo lloró a gritos.
es.R: Cuando el ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} terminó de decir estas palabras a todos los israelitas, el pueblo se puso a llorar y a lamentarse en voz alta.

fr.B: Dès que l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} eut fini de dire ces paroles à tous les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, le peuple poussa de grands cris et pleura.
fr.R: Quand l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} a fini de dire ces paroles à tous les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, le peuple s’est mis à pleurer et à se lamenter très fort.

pt.R: Quando o anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} terminou de dizer estas palavras a todos os israelitas, o povo começou a chorar e a se lamentar bem alto.

decisions.choice: lifted up their voice and wept: loud mourning
decisions.reason: To lift up the voice and weep is to cry out loud in grief (Genesis 21:16; 27:38; Judges 21:2). The people grieve at the sentence; the chapter does not say that they changed their ways, and verses 11-19 show that the next generation did not.

decisions.reason: The words are spoken to the people as a whole, as at the covenant gatherings of Joshua 8:33-35 and 24:1. The whole nation hears the charge.

decisions.choice: verses 6-9 retell Joshua 24:28-31: a step back in time
decisions.reason: Joshua's death was already mentioned in 1:1. Verses 6-9 go back to the end of his life in nearly the same words as Joshua 24:28-31, to set up what follows: the people stayed faithful while Joshua and the elders lived (verse 7), and the next generation did not (verse 10). The sending away is the end of the covenant gathering at Shechem (Joshua 24:1-27).

decisions.choice: each to his inheritance: the share of land given to each tribe and family
decisions.reason: The land was divided among the tribes and their clans by lot (Joshua 13-19). An inheritance was a family's land, held from generation to generation.

decisions.choice: take possession of the land: occupy and hold their share
decisions.reason: Each tribe still had to settle its share and drive out those living in it, as chapter 1 shows.

decisions.choice: had sent ... had gone / Earlier
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "had" and Readable adds "Earlier" so the reader sees that these verses look back to the time before 1:1.

decisions.choice: each family
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "each [man] to his inheritance". Literal and Balanced use the gender setting as Joshua 24:28 does; land was held by families, so Readable says "each family".

decisions.choice: "heredad" for the inheritance of land; "cada uno" with no gender span
decisions.reason: For the whole of Judges, as the terms note for these books sets: "heredad" is the share of land handed down in a family (m2). Spanish "cada uno" already takes in men and women, so the English gender span has no second wording in Spanish.

decisions.choice: "chacun dans son héritage" with no gender setting
alternatives: a gender setting as in the English ("each to their" / "each man to his")
decisions.reason: French "chacun" already means each person, man or woman, and "son" agrees with the land, not with the owner, so French needs no setting where the English has one, as the French style guide says for generic pronouns.

decisions.choice: "각자" / "저마다" / "집안마다" for "each to his inheritance", with no gender setting
alternatives: a gender setting as the English has
decisions.reason: Korean says "each one" without a word for "man", so the inclusive sense needs no setting. "유산" (inheritance) is the word the terms of this translation set for the land each family received.

decisions.choice: "sản nghiệp" (L, B); "phần đất mình đã được chia" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's word for the inheritance of land (m2); Readable says plainly what it is. Vietnamese "mỗi người" (each person) is already inclusive, so the gender setting of the English is not needed.

decisions.choice: cada um, with no gender setting; the wording of Joshua 24:28
decisions.reason: Verses 6-9 retell Joshua 24:28-31 (m1), so the Portuguese keeps those verses' wording where the Hebrew is the same. "Cada um" already takes in everyone, as Joshua 24:28 says in Portuguese, so there is nothing for the English gender setting to change.

source.text: וַיַּעַבְד֤וּ הָעָם֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֣י יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ וְכֹ֣ל׀יְמֵ֣י הַזְּקֵנִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֶאֱרִ֤יכוּ יָמִים֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י יְהוֹשׁ֔וּעַ אֲשֶׁ֣ר רָא֗וּ אֵ֣ת כָּל־מַעֲשֵׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ הַגָּד֔וֹל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And served the people YHWH all [the] days of Joshua and all [the] days of the elders who prolonged days after Joshua, who had seen all [the] great work of YHWH which he had done for Israel.

en.L: And the people served {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders who prolonged days after Joshua, who had seen all the great work of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done for Israel.
en.B: The people served {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all through Joshua's lifetime, and through the lifetime of the elders who lived on after him and had seen every great deed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had done for Israel.
en.R: The people served {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as long as Joshua was alive. They kept serving {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} while the older leaders who lived longer than Joshua were still alive. These leaders had seen for themselves all the great things {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had done for Israel.

sw.L: Nao watu wakamtumikia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} siku zote za Yoshua, na siku zote za wazee walioishi siku nyingi baada ya Yoshua, walioiona kazi yote kubwa ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyomfanyia Israeli.
sw.B: Watu walimtumikia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} muda wote wa maisha ya Yoshua, na muda wote wa maisha ya wazee walioishi baada yake, waliokuwa wameona kila tendo kuu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alilowatendea Israeli.
sw.R: Watu walimtumikia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} muda wote Yoshua alipokuwa hai. Waliendelea kumtumikia muda wote viongozi wazee walioishi baada ya Yoshua walipokuwa hai. Viongozi hao walikuwa wameona kwa macho yao mambo yote makuu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyowatendea Israeli.

es.L: Y el pueblo sirvió {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} todos los días de Josué y todos los días de los ancianos que prolongaron [sus] días después de Josué, que habían visto toda la gran obra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} había hecho por Israel.
es.B: El pueblo sirvió {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} durante toda la vida de Josué y durante la vida de los ancianos que vivieron más que él y que habían visto todas las grandes obras que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había hecho por Israel.
es.R: El pueblo sirvió {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} mientras Josué vivió. Lo siguieron sirviendo mientras vivieron los líderes mayores que vivieron más que Josué. Estos líderes habían visto con sus propios ojos todas las grandes cosas que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había hecho por Israel.

fr.L: Et le peuple servit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} pendant tous les jours de Josué et tous les jours des anciens qui prolongèrent [leurs] jours après Josué, qui avaient vu toute la grande œuvre {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait faite pour Israël.
fr.B: Le peuple servit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} pendant toute la vie de Josué, et pendant toute la vie des anciens qui lui survécurent et qui avaient vu toutes les grandes actions que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait accomplies pour Israël.
fr.R: Le peuple a servi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} tant que Josué a vécu. Il a continué à {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servir tant que vivaient les anciens qui avaient vécu plus longtemps que Josué. Ces anciens avaient vu de leurs propres yeux toutes les grandes choses que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait faites pour Israël.

vi.L: Và dân chúng phụng sự {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trọn các ngày của Giô-suê, và trọn các ngày của các trưởng lão sống lâu hơn Giô-suê, là những người đã thấy mọi công việc lớn lao của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm cho Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Dân chúng phụng sự {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} suốt đời Giô-suê, và suốt đời các trưởng lão sống lâu hơn ông, là những người đã thấy mọi việc lớn lao {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã làm cho Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Dân chúng phụng sự {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} suốt thời gian Giô-suê còn sống. Họ tiếp tục phụng sự {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong khi các bậc lãnh đạo lớn tuổi sống lâu hơn Giô-suê vẫn còn sống. Những người này đã tận mắt thấy mọi việc lớn lao {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã làm cho Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 그리고 백성이 여호수아의 모든 날 동안, 그리고 여호수아 뒤에 오래 살아서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘을 위하여 행하신 모든 큰일을 본 장로들의 모든 날 동안 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 섬겼다.
ko.B: 백성은 여호수아가 사는 동안 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 섬겼고, 여호수아보다 오래 살면서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘을 위하여 하신 큰일을 모두 본 장로들이 사는 동안에도 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 섬겼다.
ko.R: 여호수아가 살아 있는 동안 백성은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 섬겼다. 여호수아보다 오래 산 나이 든 지도자들이 살아 있는 동안에도 그들은 주님을 섬겼다. 이 지도자들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘을 위하여 하신 모든 큰일을 자기 눈으로 본 사람들이었다.

pt.L: E o povo serviu {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} todos os dias de Josué e todos os dias dos anciãos que prolongaram [os seus] dias depois de Josué, que tinham visto toda a grande obra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tinha feito por Israel.
pt.B: O povo serviu {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} durante toda a vida de Josué e durante toda a vida dos anciãos que viveram mais do que ele e que tinham visto todos os grandes feitos que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha realizado por Israel.
pt.R: O povo serviu {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} enquanto Josué estava vivo. E continuou servindo a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} enquanto estavam vivos os líderes mais velhos que viveram mais tempo do que Josué. Esses líderes tinham visto com os próprios olhos todas as grandes coisas que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha feito por Israel.

decisions.choice: served the LORD: worshiped him alone and obeyed him
decisions.reason: "Serve" is the word Joshua used when he called the people to choose whom they would serve (Joshua 24:14-24). It means worship and loyal obedience. The same verb returns in verse 11, where Israel serves the Baals.

decisions.choice: prolonged days after Joshua: outlived him
decisions.reason: To lengthen one's days is to live long. These elders lived on after Joshua died.

decisions.choice: all the great work of the LORD: everything God had done for Israel, seen with their own eyes
decisions.reason: The singular "work" gathers all God's acts into one: the rescue from Egypt, the crossing of the Jordan, the victories in Canaan. These elders had seen it themselves; the next generation had not (verse 10). Deuteronomy 11:7 makes the same point about the generation of the exodus.

decisions.choice: the older leaders
decisions.reason: The elders were the senior men who led the tribes and towns. Readable says "older leaders", since "elders" may suggest church officers.

decisions.choice: no deity pronoun span where the English Readable has "him" for the LORD: "Lo siguieron sirviendo"
alternatives: "Siguieron sirviéndolo a él", to carry the span on "él"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Judges, as in the Pentateuch: the deity pronoun setting goes only on pronouns Spanish writes as separate words (él, lo, le, su, mí, me, tú, te, ti, tu). Here the pronoun begins the sentence, where it is capitalized either way, so it carries no span; elsewhere a pronoun joined to a verb carries none either.

decisions.choice: "phụng sự" for serving the LORD
decisions.reason: Serving the LORD is worship and obedience together (m1); "phụng sự" says both and is kept through these chapters, also where Israel serves the Baals.

source.text: וַיָּ֛מָת יְהוֹשֻׁ֥עַ בִּן־נ֖וּן עֶ֣בֶד יְהוָ֑ה בֶּן־מֵאָ֥ה וָעֶ֖שֶׂר שָׁנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And died Joshua son of Nun, [the] slave of YHWH, a son of a hundred and ten years.

en.L: And Joshua son of Nun, the slave of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, died, a son of 110 years.
en.B: Joshua son of Nun, the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, died at 110 years of age.
en.R: Then Joshua son of Nun died. He was the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and he was 110 years old.

sw.L: Naye Yoshua mwana wa Nuni, mtumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akafa, mwana wa miaka mia na kumi.
sw.B: Yoshua mwana wa Nuni, mtumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, alikufa akiwa na umri wa miaka mia na kumi.
sw.R: Kisha Yoshua mwana wa Nuni alikufa. Alikuwa mtumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, naye alikuwa na umri wa miaka mia na kumi.

es.L: Y murió Josué hijo de Nun, siervo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, a la edad de ciento diez años.
es.B: Josué hijo de Nun, siervo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, murió a los ciento diez años de edad.
es.R: Entonces murió Josué hijo de Nun. Era el siervo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y tenía ciento diez años.

fr.L: Et Josué, fils de Noun, l’esclave {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, mourut, fils de cent dix ans.
fr.B: Josué, fils de Noun, le serviteur {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, mourut à l’âge de cent dix ans.
fr.R: Puis Josué, fils de Noun, est mort. Il était le serviteur {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et il avait cent dix ans.

vi.L: Và Giô-suê con trai Nun, đầy tớ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, qua đời, một trăm mười tuổi.
vi.B: Giô-suê con trai Nun, đầy tớ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, qua đời lúc được một trăm mười tuổi.
vi.R: Rồi Giô-suê con trai Nun qua đời. Ông là đầy tớ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và ông được một trăm mười tuổi.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 종, 눈의 아들 여호수아가 백십 세에 죽었다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 종, 눈의 아들 여호수아가 백십 세에 죽었다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 눈의 아들 여호수아가 죽었다. 그는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 종이었고, 그때 나이가 백십 세였다.

pt.L: E Josué, filho de Num, o escravo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, morreu, filho de 110 anos.
pt.B: Josué, filho de Num, o servo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, morreu com 110 anos de idade.
pt.R: Então Josué, filho de Num, morreu. Ele era o servo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} e tinha 110 anos.

decisions.choice: the slave of the LORD: Joshua's title at his death, as Moses' was at his
decisions.reason: The word is the word for a slave, one owned by a master and wholly at his disposal. Said of a man and God it is a title of honor. Moses is called this at his death (Deuteronomy 34:5); Joshua, once Moses' assistant (Joshua 1:1), receives the same title at his (Joshua 24:29).

decisions.choice: a son of 110 years: 110 years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as "a son of" so many years. Joseph also died at 110 (Genesis 50:26).

decisions.choice: slave (Literal) / servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As the style guide has it for this title: Literal shows the hard sense of the word, and Balanced and Readable say "servant", since "slave" would call to mind modern chattel slavery.

decisions.choice: "mtumishi wa BWANA" at every level, Literal included
decisions.reason: The English Literal says "slave" here, by its rule for the Hebrew word. The terms note for these books keeps "mtumishi" at every level for the title "servant of the LORD", as the Swahili Pentateuch and Psalms do for Moses: in Swahili "mtumwa wa BWANA" would sound like ownership, while the title speaks of a trusted servant.

decisions.choice: "siervo del SEÑOR" at every level
alternatives: "esclavo del SEÑOR" at Literal, as the English Literal "slave"
decisions.reason: As the terms note for these books sets: the title given to Moses and to Joshua at his death is "siervo" at every level, as in Psalms. "Esclavo" in Spanish would suggest only forced labor, while the title names a man who belongs wholly to the LORD's service (m1). The Literal "a son of 110 years" is said in Spanish as "a la edad de ciento diez años".

decisions.choice: "l'esclave" (L); "le serviteur" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch note sets for *eved*: "esclave" at Literal, "serviteur" at Balanced and Readable, as the English has "slave" and "servant". It is a title of honour here, given to Joshua at his death as it was to Moses (Joshua 24:29).

decisions.choice: "đầy tớ" at every level
decisions.reason: The Genesis note keeps "đầy tớ" for the servant of the LORD and "nô lệ" for slavery itself; the title is one of honour (m1), as for Moses.

decisions.choice: "một trăm mười tuổi" at Literal
decisions.reason: Vietnamese cannot say "a son of 110 years"; this is the ordinary way of giving an age (m2).

decisions.choice: "종" for *eved* at every level
decisions.reason: Korean "종" covers both slave and servant, and it is the title Moses has in this translation; "노예" is kept for slavery itself, as the terms of this translation set.

source.text: וַיִּקְבְּר֤וּ אוֹתוֹ֙ בִּגְב֣וּל נַחֲלָת֔וֹ בְּתִמְנַת־חֶ֖רֶס בְּהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם מִצְּפ֖וֹן לְהַר־גָּֽעַשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they buried him in [the] territory of his inheritance in Timnath-heres in [the] hill country of Ephraim, from [the] north of [the] mountain of Gaash.

en.L: And they buried him in the territory of his inheritance, at Timnath-heres, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of the mountain of Gaash.
en.B: They buried him within the borders of his own inheritance, at Timnath-heres, north of Mount Gaash in the hill country of Ephraim.
en.R: He was buried on his own land at Timnath-heres. It is in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.

sw.L: Nao wakamzika katika mpaka wa urithi wake, huko Timnath-heresi, katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu, kaskazini mwa mlima wa Gaashi.
sw.B: Walimzika ndani ya mipaka ya urithi wake mwenyewe, huko Timnath-heresi, kaskazini mwa Mlima Gaashi katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu.
sw.R: Alizikwa katika nchi yake mwenyewe huko Timnath-heresi. Mahali hapo ni katika nchi ya milima ya Efraimu, kaskazini mwa Mlima Gaashi.

es.L: Y lo sepultaron en el territorio de su heredad, en Timnat-heres, en la región montañosa de Efraín, al norte del monte Gaas.
es.B: Lo sepultaron dentro de los límites de su propia heredad, en Timnat-heres, al norte del monte Gaas, en la región montañosa de Efraín.
es.R: Lo enterraron en su propia tierra, en Timnat-heres. Está en la región montañosa de Efraín, al norte del monte Gaas.

fr.L: Et ils l’enterrèrent dans le territoire de son héritage, à Timnath-Hérès, dans la montagne d’Éphraïm, au nord de la montagne de Gaash.
fr.B: On l’enterra dans les limites de son propre héritage, à Timnath-Hérès, au nord du mont Gaash, dans la région montagneuse d’Éphraïm.
fr.R: On l’a enterré sur sa propre terre, à Timnath-Hérès. C’est dans la région des collines d’Éphraïm, au nord du mont Gaash.

vi.L: Và họ chôn ông trong địa phận sản nghiệp của ông, tại Thim-nát-Hê-re, trong vùng đồi núi Ép-ra-im, ở phía bắc núi Ga-ách.
vi.B: Họ chôn ông trong ranh giới sản nghiệp của ông, tại Thim-nát-Hê-re, phía bắc núi Ga-ách, trong vùng đồi núi Ép-ra-im.
vi.R: Ông được chôn trên phần đất của mình tại Thim-nát-Hê-re. Nơi ấy ở vùng đồi núi Ép-ra-im, phía bắc núi Ga-ách.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 그를 그의 유산의 경계 안, 가아스 산 북쪽, 에브라임 산지에 있는 딤낫헤레스에 묻었다.
ko.B: 사람들은 그를 그가 유산으로 받은 땅, 에브라임 산지 가아스 산 북쪽에 있는 딤낫헤레스에 묻었다.
ko.R: 여호수아는 자기가 받은 땅 딤낫헤레스에 묻혔다. 그곳은 에브라임 산지에 있는 가아스 산 북쪽이다.

pt.L: E o sepultaram no território da sua herança, em Timnate-Heres, na região montanhosa de Efraim, ao norte do monte Gaás.
pt.B: Eles o sepultaram dentro dos limites da sua própria herança, em Timnate-Heres, ao norte do monte Gaás, na região montanhosa de Efraim.
pt.R: Ele foi sepultado na sua própria terra, em Timnate-Heres. Esse lugar fica na região montanhosa de Efraim, ao norte do monte Gaás.

decisions.choice: Timnath-heres: the town called Timnath-serah in Joshua
decisions.reason: Joshua's town is called Timnath-serah in Joshua 19:50 and 24:30. Here the last letters stand in the reverse order, which gives "heres", a rare word for "sun". It is the same place; the two spellings are kept as each book has them.

decisions.choice: the territory of his inheritance: the town given to Joshua himself
decisions.reason: When the land was divided, the Israelites gave Joshua the town he asked for, in the hill country of Ephraim, his own tribe (Joshua 19:49-50). He was buried on the land he had received.

decisions.choice: He was buried
decisions.reason: "They buried him" names no one in particular, so Readable uses the passive; Balanced keeps the wording of Joshua 24:30.

decisions.choice: Timnate-Heres
decisions.reason: The town is spelled as this verse has it (m1), with the Brazilian pattern Joshua 24:30 uses for "Timnate-Sera", so that the two spellings stay as each book has them, as in the English.

source.text: וְגַם֙ כָּל־הַדּ֣וֹר הַה֔וּא נֶאֶסְפ֖וּ אֶל־אֲבוֹתָ֑יו וַיָּקָם֩ דּ֨וֹר אַחֵ֜ר אַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹא־יָֽדְעוּ֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה וְגַם֙ אֶת־הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And also all that generation were gathered to its fathers, and arose another generation after them who not knew YHWH and also the work which he had done for Israel.

en.L: And also all that generation was gathered to their fathers, and another generation arose after them who did not know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, nor the work that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done for Israel.
en.B: That whole generation also died and was gathered to their {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}, and after them another generation grew up who did not know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} or what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done for Israel.
en.R: In time, everyone in that generation died. The next generation did not know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They did not know the things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done for Israel.

sw.L: Na pia kizazi kile chote kikakusanywa kwa baba zao, na kizazi kingine kikainuka baada yao ambacho hakikumjua {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wala kazi aliyomfanyia Israeli.
sw.B: Kizazi kile chote nacho kilikufa na kukusanywa kwa mababu zao, na baada yao kikakua kizazi kingine ambacho hakikumjua {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wala kile alichowatendea Israeli.
sw.R: Baada ya muda, watu wote wa kizazi kile walikufa. Kizazi kilichofuata hakikumjua {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Hakikujua mambo aliyowatendea Israeli.

es.L: Y también toda aquella generación fue reunida con sus padres, y se levantó después de ellos otra generación que no conocía {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, ni la obra que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} había hecho por Israel.
es.B: También toda aquella generación murió y fue reunida con sus antepasados, y después de ellos creció otra generación que no conocía {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} ni lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} había hecho por Israel.
es.R: Con el tiempo, murieron todos los de aquella generación. La generación siguiente no conocía {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. No sabían las cosas que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} había hecho por Israel.

fr.L: Et toute cette génération aussi fut réunie à ses pères, et une autre génération se leva après eux, qui ne connaissait pas {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, ni l’œuvre qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait faite pour Israël.
fr.B: Toute cette génération mourut à son tour et fut réunie à ses {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}, et après eux grandit une autre génération qui ne connaissait pas {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, ni ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait fait pour Israël.
fr.R: Avec le temps, tous les gens de cette génération sont morts. La génération suivante ne connaissait pas {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Elle ne connaissait pas les choses qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait faites pour Israël.

vi.L: Và cả thế hệ ấy cũng được tụ về với tổ phụ mình, và một thế hệ khác nổi lên sau họ, không biết {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, cũng không biết công việc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm cho Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Cả thế hệ ấy cũng qua đời và được tụ về với tổ tiên mình. Sau họ, một thế hệ khác lớn lên, không biết {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, cũng không biết những gì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm cho Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Theo thời gian, mọi người trong thế hệ ấy đều qua đời. Thế hệ sau không biết {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Họ không biết những việc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm cho Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 그리고 그 세대도 모두 그들의 조상들에게로 모여 갔고, 그들 뒤에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 알지 못하고 그분께서 이스라엘을 위하여 행하신 일도 알지 못하는 다른 세대가 일어났다.
ko.B: 그 세대 사람들도 모두 죽어 조상들에게로 돌아갔다. 그리고 그 뒤에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 알지 못하고, 그분께서 이스라엘을 위하여 하신 일도 알지 못하는 다른 세대가 자라났다.
ko.R: 시간이 흘러 그 세대 사람들도 모두 죽었다. 다음 세대는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 알지 못하였다. 그들은 주님께서 이스라엘을 위하여 하신 일들도 알지 못하였다.

pt.L: E também toda aquela geração foi reunida aos seus pais, e outra geração se levantou depois deles, que não conhecia {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, nem a obra que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tinha feito por Israel.
pt.B: Toda aquela geração também morreu e foi reunida aos seus {{gender:antepassados|pais}}, e depois dela cresceu outra geração, que não conhecia {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} nem o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tinha feito por Israel.
pt.R: Com o tempo, todas as pessoas daquela geração morreram. A geração seguinte não conhecia {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. Não sabia das coisas que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tinha feito por Israel.

decisions.choice: gathered to their fathers: died and joined the generations before them
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of death (Genesis 25:8; 49:33; Numbers 20:24). It pictures the dead as joining their own people who died before them.

decisions.choice: did not know the LORD: had no personal knowledge of him and did not acknowledge him
decisions.reason: To "know" the LORD is more than knowing about him: it is to know him by experience and to honor him (Exodus 5:2; 1 Samuel 2:12; 3:7). This generation had not seen God's great work (contrast verse 7) and did not hold to him.

decisions.choice: another generation: the failure to pass on what God had done
decisions.reason: Moses had told Israel to teach their children what God had done (Deuteronomy 4:9-10; 6:6-7, 20-25). The new generation's ignorance is the start of the pattern of verses 11-19.

decisions.choice: died
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the picture of being gathered to one's ancestors means.

decisions.choice: "tổ phụ" (L); "tổ tiên" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "tổ tiên" (ancestors) includes the mothers of Israel, as the English gender setting's default does; Literal keeps "tổ phụ" (fathers), as the English Literal says "fathers". Vietnamese needs no setting span for this.

source.text: וַיַּעֲשׂ֧וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת־הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּעַבְד֖וּ אֶת־הַבְּעָלִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And did [the] sons of Israel the evil in [the] eyes of YHWH, and they served the Baals.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and served the Baals.
en.B: Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and served the Baals.
en.R: Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. They worshiped the Baals, the gods of the Canaanites.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakafanya maovu machoni pa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wakawatumikia Mabaali.
sw.B: Kisha Waisraeli walifanya maovu machoni pa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wakawatumikia Mabaali.
sw.R: Kisha Waisraeli walifanya yale ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alisema ni maovu. Waliwaabudu Mabaali, miungu ya Wakanaani.

es.L: Y los hijos de Israel hicieron lo malo a los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y sirvieron a los baales.
es.B: Entonces los israelitas hicieron lo malo a los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y sirvieron a los baales.
es.R: Entonces los israelitas hicieron lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había dicho que era malo. Adoraron a los baales, los dioses de los cananeos.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël firent le mal aux yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et ils servirent les Baals.
fr.B: Alors les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} firent ce qui est mal aux yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et servirent les Baals.
fr.R: Alors les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont fait ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} déclarait mauvais. Ils ont adoré les Baals, les dieux des Cananéens.

vi.L: Và con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên làm điều ác trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và phụng sự các Ba-anh.
vi.B: Rồi dân Y-sơ-ra-ên làm điều ác trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và phụng sự các thần Ba-anh.
vi.R: Rồi dân Y-sơ-ra-ên làm điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho là ác. Họ thờ các thần Ba-anh, là các thần của người Ca-na-an.

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘 자손이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 보시기에 악한 일을 하였고, 바알들을 섬겼다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 이스라엘 백성은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 보시기에 악한 일을 하였고, 바알들을 섬겼다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 이스라엘 백성은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 악하다고 하신 일을 하였다. 그들은 가나안 사람들의 신인 바알들을 섬겼다.

pt.L: E os filhos de Israel fizeram o mal aos olhos {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} e serviram os baalins.
pt.B: Então os israelitas fizeram o que era mau aos olhos {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} e serviram os baalins.
pt.R: Então os israelitas fizeram o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} considerava mau. Eles adoraram os baalins, os deuses dos cananeus.

decisions.choice: did the evil in the eyes of the LORD: did what the LORD judged to be evil
decisions.reason: "In the eyes of" someone means by their judgment. The standard is the LORD's, not the people's own (compare 17:6; 21:25, where each did what was right in his own eyes). This sentence opens the pattern that runs through the book (3:7, 12; 4:1; 6:1; 10:6; 13:1), and here the evil is named at once: the worship of other gods.

decisions.choice: the Baals: the many local forms of the god Baal
decisions.reason: Baal, "lord" or "master", was the Canaanite god of storm and rain, worshiped for the fertility of fields and herds. He was honored under many local names and at many shrines, such as the Baal of Peor (Numbers 25:3) and Baal-berith (Judges 8:33); the plural gathers them all.

decisions.choice: served the Baals: the service owed to the LORD given to other gods
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in verse 7 for serving the LORD. Israel did not merely add a ritual; they changed masters.

decisions.choice: did what the LORD said was evil
alternatives: did evil in the LORD's sight
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that the LORD is the judge of what is evil, which is what "in the eyes of the LORD" means.

decisions.choice: worshiped ... the gods of the Canaanites
decisions.reason: Readable says "worshiped" for "served" here and explains who the Baals were.

decisions.choice: "walifanya maovu machoni pa BWANA" (L, B); "walifanya yale ambayo BWANA alisema ni maovu" (R), through the book
decisions.reason: The formula that opens each cycle of Judges keeps the Hebrew picture "in the eyes of" at Literal and Balanced, as the terms note sets; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does. The Baals are "Mabaali", the plural of "Baali".

decisions.choice: "hicieron lo malo a los ojos del SEÑOR" (L, B); "hicieron lo que el SEÑOR había dicho que era malo" (R); "los baales"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Judges, as the terms note for these books sets: the phrase that opens each round of the book keeps the Hebrew picture of the LORD's eyes at Literal and Balanced; Readable says what it means (m1). The many local forms of Baal are "los baales", in lowercase as a common plural (m2).

decisions.choice: "le mal aux yeux du SEIGNEUR" (L); "ce qui est mal aux yeux du SEIGNEUR" (B); "ce que le SEIGNEUR déclarait mauvais" (R)
decisions.reason: For Judges 1-10, where the phrase opens each new cycle (3:7, 3:12, 4:1, 6:1, 10:6): the terms note sets "ce qui est mal aux yeux du SEIGNEUR". Literal keeps the Hebrew article, "le mal"; Readable says plainly that it is the LORD who judges it evil, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "les Baals"; "les Astartés" for the Ashtaroth (2:13), "les Ashéras" for the Asherahs (3:7)
decisions.reason: For Judges 1-10, as the terms note sets: the plural names the many local forms of Baal; the goddesses take their French names. They are written with a capital, as names.

decisions.choice: "주께서 보시기에 악한 일을 하였다" (L, B); "주께서 악하다고 하신 일을 하였다" (R)
alternatives: "주의 눈앞에서 악을 행하였다", closer to the Hebrew picture of the eyes
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set for this refrain of Judges, so that it reads the same each time it returns; "보시기에" keeps the Hebrew's "in the eyes of" in ordinary Korean. Readable says plainly that the LORD judged it evil, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "làm điều ác trước mặt CHÚA" (L, B); "làm điều CHÚA cho là ác" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's wording for this refrain of the book (m1); Readable says whose judgment it is, as the English Readable does. The same words are kept each time it returns.

decisions.choice: "các Ba-anh" (L); "các thần Ba-anh" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The plural is the many local forms of Baal (m2); the terms note's form.

decisions.choice: fizeram o mal aos olhos do SENHOR (L); fizeram o que era mau aos olhos do SENHOR (B); fizeram o que o SENHOR considerava mau (R)
alternatives: praticaram o mal perante o SENHOR
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the sentence that opens each round of the cycle (m1; 3:7, 12; 4:1; 6:1; 10:6; 13:1) keeps one wording at each level, that of Deuteronomy 4:25 and 31:29 in Portuguese. Readable says plainly that the LORD is the judge, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: os baalins (the Baals); Baal (one god)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 3:7; 8:33; 10:6, 10): the plural of the god's name (m2) is the traditional Portuguese "baalins", written lower case as a word for many local gods; the god himself is "Baal". Readable adds who they were, as the English does.

source.text: וַיַּעַזְב֞וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה׀אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבוֹתָ֗ם הַמּוֹצִ֣יא אוֹתָם֮ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַיִם֒ וַיֵּלְכ֞וּ אַחֲרֵ֣י׀אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֗ים מֵאֱלֹהֵ֤י הָֽעַמִּים֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ סְבִיב֣וֹתֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם וַיַּכְעִ֖סוּ אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they forsook YHWH, [the] God of their fathers, the [one] bringing out them from [the] land of Egypt, and they went after other gods, from [the] gods of the peoples who [were] around them, and they bowed down to them, and they provoked to anger YHWH.

en.L: And they forsook {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and went after other gods, from the gods of the peoples who [were] around them, and bowed down to them, and provoked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to anger.
en.B: They abandoned {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt. They followed other gods, gods of the peoples who lived around them, and bowed down to them, and so they made {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} angry.
en.R: They turned away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God their {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} had worshiped, the God who had brought them out of Egypt. They followed other gods, the gods of the nations all around them. They bowed down to those gods, and this made {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} angry.

sw.L: Nao wakamwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa baba zao, aliyewatoa katika nchi ya Misri, wakaifuata miungu mingine, katika miungu ya mataifa yaliyowazunguka, wakaisujudia, wakamkasirisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Walimwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa mababu zao, aliyekuwa amewatoa katika nchi ya Misri. Waliifuata miungu mingine, miungu ya mataifa yaliyowazunguka, wakaisujudia, na hivyo wakamkasirisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Walimgeuka {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu ambaye mababu zao walimwabudu, Mungu aliyewatoa Misri. Waliifuata miungu mingine, miungu ya mataifa yaliyowazunguka pande zote. Waliisujudia miungu hiyo, na jambo hilo likamkasirisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

es.L: Y abandonaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, el Dios de sus padres, que los había sacado de la tierra de Egipto, y fueron tras otros dioses, de los dioses de los pueblos que [estaban] alrededor de ellos, y se postraron ante ellos, y provocaron a ira {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.B: Abandonaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, el Dios de sus antepasados, que los había sacado de la tierra de Egipto. Siguieron a otros dioses, dioses de los pueblos que vivían a su alrededor, y se postraron ante ellos, y así hicieron enojar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.R: Se apartaron {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, el Dios a quien habían adorado sus antepasados, el Dios que los había sacado de Egipto. Siguieron a otros dioses, los dioses de las naciones que los rodeaban. Se inclinaron ante esos dioses, y esto hizo enojar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et ils abandonnèrent {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu de leurs pères, qui les avait fait sortir du pays d’Égypte, et ils allèrent après d’autres dieux, parmi les dieux des peuples qui [étaient] autour d’eux, et ils se prosternèrent devant eux, et ils irritèrent {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Ils abandonnèrent {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu de leurs {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}, qui les avait fait sortir du pays d’Égypte. Ils suivirent d’autres dieux, des dieux des peuples qui vivaient autour d’eux, et se prosternèrent devant eux ; ainsi ils mirent {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} en colère.
fr.R: Ils se sont détournés {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, le Dieu que leurs {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} avaient adoré, le Dieu qui les avait fait sortir d’Égypte. Ils ont suivi d’autres dieux, les dieux des peuples tout autour d’eux. Ils se sont prosternés devant ces dieux, et cela a mis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} en colère.

vi.L: Và họ lìa bỏ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của tổ phụ họ, Đấng đã đem họ ra khỏi xứ Ai Cập, và đi theo các thần khác, trong các thần của các dân [ở] chung quanh họ, và cúi lạy chúng, và chọc giận {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Họ lìa bỏ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của tổ tiên họ, Đấng đã đem họ ra khỏi xứ Ai Cập. Họ đi theo các thần khác, là các thần của những dân tộc sống chung quanh họ, và cúi lạy các thần ấy, nên họ chọc giận {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Họ quay lưng với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, là Đức Chúa Trời mà tổ tiên họ đã thờ, Đấng đã đem họ ra khỏi Ai Cập. Họ đi theo các thần khác, là các thần của những dân tộc chung quanh. Họ cúi lạy các thần ấy, và việc này làm cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nổi giận.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 그들을 이집트 땅에서 이끌어 내신 그들의 조상들의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 버리고, 다른 신들, 곧 그들 주위에 있는 민족들의 신들을 따라가서 그들에게 절하였고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 노엽게 하였다.
ko.B: 그들은 자기들을 이집트 땅에서 이끌어 내신 조상들의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 버렸다. 그들은 다른 신들, 곧 주위에 사는 민족들의 신들을 따라가 그 신들에게 절하였다. 그래서 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 노하시게 하였다.
ko.R: 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게서 돌아섰다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 그들의 조상들이 섬기던 하나님이시며, 그들을 이집트에서 이끌어 내신 하나님이셨다. 그들은 주위의 모든 민족이 섬기는 다른 신들을 따라갔다. 그 신들에게 절하였고, 이 일로 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 노하셨다.

pt.L: E abandonaram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus dos seus pais, que os tirou da terra do Egito, e foram atrás de outros deuses, dos deuses dos povos que [estavam] ao redor deles, e se prostraram diante deles, e provocaram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} à ira.
pt.B: Eles abandonaram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus dos seus {{gender:antepassados|pais}}, que os tinha tirado da terra do Egito. Seguiram outros deuses, deuses dos povos que viviam ao redor deles, e se prostraram diante deles, e assim deixaram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} irado.
pt.R: Eles se afastaram {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o Deus que os seus {{gender:antepassados|pais}} tinham adorado, o Deus que os tinha tirado do Egito. Seguiram outros deuses, os deuses das nações ao seu redor. Eles se curvaram diante desses deuses, e isso deixou {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} irado.

decisions.choice: forsook the LORD, who brought them out of Egypt: turning from the God who had saved them
decisions.reason: The first commandment rests on the same words: "I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt ... you shall have no other gods" (Exodus 20:2-3). Israel had promised never to forsake the LORD for other gods (Joshua 24:16-18), and Moses had warned that they would (Deuteronomy 31:16).

decisions.choice: went after other gods: followed them as their worshipers
decisions.reason: To "go after" a god is to follow it as a servant follows a master (Deuteronomy 6:14; 8:19).

decisions.choice: provoked the LORD to anger: gave him cause for anger
decisions.reason: The verb means to vex or offend. Worship of other gods is what provokes the LORD in Deuteronomy 4:25 and 31:29; verse 14 gives his response.

decisions.choice: the God their ancestors had worshiped
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the God of their ancestors": the God their families had always served.

source.text: וַיַּעַזְב֖וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּעַבְד֥וּ לַבַּ֖עַל וְלָעַשְׁתָּרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And they forsook YHWH and they served the Baal and the Ashtaroth.

en.L: And they forsook {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and served Baal and the Ashtaroth.
en.B: They abandoned {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and served Baal and the Ashtaroth.
en.R: They left {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and worshiped Baal and the goddesses called the Ashtaroth.

sw.L: Nao wakamwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wakamtumikia Baali na Maashtorethi.
sw.B: Walimwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wakamtumikia Baali na Maashtorethi.
sw.R: Walimwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wakamwabudu Baali na miungu ya kike iitwayo Maashtorethi.

es.L: Y abandonaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y sirvieron a Baal y a las astartés.
es.B: Abandonaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y sirvieron a Baal y a las astartés.
es.R: Dejaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y adoraron a Baal y a las diosas llamadas astartés.

fr.L: Et ils abandonnèrent {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et ils servirent Baal et les Astartés.
fr.B: Ils abandonnèrent {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et servirent Baal et les Astartés.
fr.R: Ils ont quitté {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et ont adoré Baal et les déesses qu’on appelle les Astartés.

vi.L: Và họ lìa bỏ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và phụng sự Ba-anh và các Át-tạt-tê.
vi.B: Họ lìa bỏ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và phụng sự thần Ba-anh và các nữ thần Át-tạt-tê.
vi.R: Họ bỏ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và thờ thần Ba-anh cùng các nữ thần gọi là Át-tạt-tê.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 버리고 바알과 아스다롯을 섬겼다.
ko.B: 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 버리고 바알과 아스다롯을 섬겼다.
ko.R: 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 떠나 바알과, 아스다롯이라고 불리는 여신들을 섬겼다.

pt.L: E abandonaram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} e serviram Baal e Astarote.
pt.B: Eles abandonaram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} e serviram Baal e Astarote.
pt.R: Eles deixaram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} e adoraram Baal e as várias formas da deusa Astarote.

decisions.choice: Baal and the Ashtaroth: the gods and goddesses of Canaan
decisions.reason: Ashtaroth is the plural of Ashtoreth (1 Kings 11:5), a Canaanite goddess of fertility and war, worshiped beside Baal. Like "the Baals", the plural takes in her many local forms. Together the pair stands for the whole of Canaanite religion (10:6; 1 Samuel 7:4; 12:10).

decisions.choice: they forsook the LORD: said again for emphasis
decisions.reason: Verse 12 has already said that they forsook the LORD. The repetition sets the leaving of the LORD and the serving of other gods side by side: the one meant the other.

decisions.choice: the goddesses called the Ashtaroth
decisions.reason: Readable says what the name refers to, as m1 explains.

decisions.choice: "las astartés"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Judges, as the terms note for these books sets: the goddesses are "las astartés", a common plural for the many local forms of the goddess Astarte, as "los baales" is for Baal; later "las aserás" for the Asherahs.

decisions.choice: Baal e Astarote (L, B); Baal e as várias formas da deusa Astarote (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 10:6): the goddess keeps the name Deuteronomy 1:4 and Joshua 9:10 give the town named after her, "Astarote", which Portuguese readers know as her name; the Hebrew plural, her many local forms (m1), is not marked at Literal and Balanced, since "as Astarotes" would read as a mistake. Readable says it, as the English Readable says "the goddesses called the Ashtaroth".

source.text: וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֤ף יְהוָה֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַֽיִּתְּנֵם֙ בְּיַד־שֹׁסִ֔ים וַיָּשֹׁ֖סּוּ אוֹתָ֑ם וַֽיִּמְכְּרֵ֞ם בְּיַ֤ד אֽוֹיְבֵיהֶם֙ מִסָּבִ֔יב וְלֹֽא־יָכְל֣וּ ע֔וֹד לַעֲמֹ֖ד לִפְנֵ֥י אוֹיְבֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And burned [the] anger of YHWH against Israel, and he gave them into [the] hand of plunderers, and they plundered them, and he sold them into [the] hand of their enemies around, and not they were able any longer to stand before their enemies.

en.L: And the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned against Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them into [the] hand of plunderers, and they plundered them; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sold them into [the] hand of their enemies all around, and they could no longer stand before their enemies.
en.B: Then the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blazed against Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them into the power of raiders, who plundered them. He sold them into the power of the enemies who surrounded them, and they could no longer hold their ground against their enemies.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} became very angry with Israel. He let raiders attack them and steal what they had. He handed them over to the enemies all around them, as a master sells a slave. Israel could no longer fight off their enemies.

sw.L: Na hasira ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ikawaka juu ya Israeli, akawatia mkononi mwa wateka nyara, nao wakawateka nyara; akawauza mkononi mwa adui zao pande zote, wala hawakuweza tena kusimama mbele ya adui zao.
sw.B: Ndipo hasira ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ikawaka dhidi ya Israeli, akawatia mikononi mwa wavamizi waliowateka nyara. Aliwauza mikononi mwa adui waliowazunguka, nao hawakuweza tena kusimama imara mbele ya adui zao.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwakasirikia Israeli sana. Aliwaacha wavamizi wawashambulie na kuwanyang'anya mali zao. Aliwatia mikononi mwa adui waliowazunguka, kama bwana anavyomuuza mtumwa. Israeli hawakuweza tena kuwashinda adui zao.

es.L: Y se encendió la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} contra Israel, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los entregó en mano de saqueadores, y los saquearon; y los vendió en mano de sus enemigos de alrededor, y ya no pudieron mantenerse en pie delante de sus enemigos.
es.B: Entonces la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se encendió contra Israel, y los entregó en poder de saqueadores, que los despojaron. Los vendió en poder de los enemigos que los rodeaban, y ya no pudieron hacer frente a sus enemigos.
es.R: Así que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se enojó mucho con Israel. Dejó que los saqueadores los atacaran y les robaran lo que tenían. Los entregó a los enemigos que había a su alrededor, como un amo vende a un esclavo. Israel ya no podía defenderse de sus enemigos.

fr.L: Et la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’enflamma contre Israël, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les livra dans la main de pillards, et ils les pillèrent ; et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les vendit dans la main de leurs ennemis tout autour, et ils ne purent plus tenir devant leurs ennemis.
fr.B: Alors la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’enflamma contre Israël, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les livra au pouvoir de pillards qui les dépouillèrent. Il les vendit au pouvoir des ennemis qui les entouraient, et ils ne purent plus résister à leurs ennemis.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} s’est mis très en colère contre Israël. Il a laissé des pillards les attaquer et leur voler ce qu’ils avaient. Il les a livrés aux ennemis qui les entouraient, comme un maître vend un esclave. Israël ne pouvait plus repousser ses ennemis.

vi.L: Và cơn giận của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nổi phừng lên cùng Y-sơ-ra-ên, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phó họ vào tay những kẻ cướp bóc, và chúng cướp bóc họ; và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bán họ vào tay các kẻ thù chung quanh, và họ không còn đứng nổi trước mặt kẻ thù mình nữa.
vi.B: Bấy giờ cơn giận của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nổi phừng lên cùng Y-sơ-ra-ên, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} giao họ cho những kẻ cướp bóc, là những kẻ cướp sạch của họ. Ngài bán họ cho các kẻ thù chung quanh, và họ không còn chống cự nổi kẻ thù nữa.
vi.R: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} rất giận Y-sơ-ra-ên. Ngài để cho những kẻ cướp tấn công họ và lấy đi những gì họ có. Ngài giao họ cho các kẻ thù chung quanh, như một người chủ bán đầy tớ của mình. Y-sơ-ra-ên không còn chống cự nổi kẻ thù nữa.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 진노가 이스라엘에게 불타올라, 그분께서 그들을 약탈자들의 손에 주시니 그들이 그들을 약탈하였다. 그리고 그분께서 그들을 주위의 원수들의 손에 파셨으므로, 그들이 더 이상 그들의 원수들 앞에 설 수 없었다.
ko.B: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘에게 크게 진노하셨다. 그분께서 그들을 약탈하는 자들의 손에 넘기시니, 그들이 이스라엘을 약탈하였다. 주님께서 그들을 사방에 있는 원수들의 손에 파셨으므로, 그들은 더 이상 원수들을 당해 낼 수 없었다.
ko.R: 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘에게 몹시 화가 나셨다. 주님께서는 약탈자들이 그들을 공격하여 그들의 것을 빼앗아 가게 하셨다. 주인이 종을 팔아넘기듯이, 그들을 사방에 있는 원수들에게 넘기셨다. 이스라엘은 더 이상 원수들을 물리칠 수 없었다.

pt.L: E a ira {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} se acendeu contra Israel, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} os entregou na mão de saqueadores, e os saquearam; e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} os vendeu na mão dos seus inimigos ao redor, e não puderam mais resistir diante dos seus inimigos.
pt.B: Então a ira {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} se inflamou contra Israel, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} os entregou ao poder de saqueadores, que os despojaram. Ele os vendeu ao poder dos inimigos que os cercavam, e eles não conseguiram mais resistir aos seus inimigos.
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} ficou muito irado com Israel. Deixou que saqueadores os atacassem e roubassem o que eles tinham. Entregou-os aos inimigos que havia ao redor, como um senhor vende um escravo. Israel não conseguia mais se defender dos seus inimigos.

decisions.choice: the anger of the LORD burned: the LORD was very angry
decisions.reason: Anger is pictured as a fire that flares up (Exodus 32:10-11; Numbers 25:3). It is the response to the provocation of verse 12.

decisions.choice: gave them into the hand of ... sold them into the hand of: handed them over to the power of
decisions.reason: "Hand" means power or control. To "sell" a people to its enemies is to give them up, as a master sells a slave and no longer protects him (Deuteronomy 32:30). Judges uses the picture again for each oppression (3:8; 4:2; 10:7).

decisions.choice: they could no longer stand before their enemies: the covenant warning come true
decisions.reason: In Joshua's time no one could stand before Israel (Joshua 1:5; 21:44). The law had warned that if Israel turned from the LORD, they would have no power to stand before their enemies (Leviticus 26:17, 37; Deuteronomy 28:25). Now the promise of victory is reversed.

decisions.choice: as a master sells a slave
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture of selling and explains it, since "sold them" alone could sound like a trade for money.

decisions.choice: "cơn giận ... nổi phừng lên cùng" (L, B); "rất giận" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew pictures anger burning (m1); Literal and Balanced keep the fire, Readable says plainly that the LORD was very angry. Kept the same where it returns.

decisions.choice: os vendeu na mão de (L); os vendeu ao poder de (B); entregou-os ..., como um senhor vende um escravo (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (3:8; 4:2, 9; 10:7): the picture of selling (m2) is kept at every level, "vender" as the Hebrew says, so that the reader hears a master giving up a slave; Readable explains it, as the English does.

source.text: בְּכֹ֣ל׀אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָצְא֗וּ יַד־יְהוָה֙ הָיְתָה־בָּ֣ם לְרָעָ֔ה כַּֽאֲשֶׁר֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה וְכַאֲשֶׁ֛ר נִשְׁבַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה לָהֶ֑ם וַיֵּ֥צֶר לָהֶ֖ם מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: In all where they went out, [the] hand of YHWH was against them for harm, as had spoken YHWH and as had sworn YHWH to them, and it was distress to them greatly.

en.L: Wherever they went out, the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was against them for harm, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken and as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had sworn to them, and they were in great distress.
en.B: Every time they went out to fight, the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was against them to bring them disaster, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had warned and had sworn to them. They were in great distress.
en.R: Every time Israel went out to battle, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was against them, and they were defeated. This was just what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had warned them about. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had promised with an oath that it would happen. So the people suffered terribly.

sw.L: Kila walipotoka, mkono wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ulikuwa dhidi yao kwa mabaya, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyosema, na kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyowaapia; nao wakawa katika dhiki kubwa.
sw.B: Kila walipotoka kwenda vitani, mkono wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ulikuwa dhidi yao kuwaletea maafa, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyowaonya na kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyowaapia. Walikuwa katika dhiki kubwa.
sw.R: Kila mara Israeli walipokwenda vitani, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa dhidi yao, nao wakashindwa. Hivyo ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa amewaonya. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa ameahidi kwa kiapo kwamba jambo hilo lingetokea. Kwa hiyo watu waliteseka sana.

es.L: Dondequiera que salían, la mano {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} estaba contra ellos para mal, como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había hablado y como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les había jurado; y estuvieron en gran angustia.
es.B: Cada vez que salían a pelear, la mano {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} estaba contra ellos para traerles desgracia, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les había advertido y jurado. Estaban en gran angustia.
es.R: Cada vez que Israel salía a la batalla, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estaba contra ellos, y eran derrotados. Era justo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les había advertido. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había prometido con juramento que sucedería. Así que el pueblo sufrió terriblemente.

fr.L: Partout où ils sortaient, la main {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} était contre eux pour le malheur, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait dit et comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} le leur avait juré ; et ils furent dans une grande détresse.
fr.B: Chaque fois qu’ils partaient au combat, la main {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} était contre eux pour leur malheur, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les en avait avertis et le leur avait juré. Ils furent dans une grande détresse.
fr.R: Chaque fois qu’Israël partait à la guerre, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} était contre eux, et ils étaient battus. C’était exactement ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur avait annoncé. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait promis par serment que cela arriverait. Le peuple a donc terriblement souffert.

vi.L: Hễ họ đi ra đâu, tay của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} chống lại họ để làm hại, như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán và như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã thề với họ; và họ bị khốn khổ lắm.
vi.B: Mỗi khi họ ra trận, tay của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} chống lại họ để giáng họa, đúng như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã cảnh báo và đã thề với họ. Họ lâm vào cảnh khốn cùng.
vi.R: Mỗi khi Y-sơ-ra-ên ra trận, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} chống lại họ, và họ bị đánh bại. Đây đúng là điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã cảnh báo họ. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã thề rằng việc ấy sẽ xảy ra. Vì vậy dân chúng chịu khổ sở vô cùng.

ko.L: 그들이 나가는 곳마다 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하신 대로, 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들에게 맹세하신 대로, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 손이 그들을 해치려고 그들을 대적하였다. 그래서 그들이 몹시 괴로웠다.
ko.B: 그들이 싸우러 나갈 때마다, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 경고하시고 맹세하신 대로 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 손이 그들을 쳐서 재앙을 내리셨다. 그래서 그들은 큰 고통을 겪었다.
ko.R: 이스라엘이 싸우러 나갈 때마다 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들을 치셨고, 그들은 싸움에서 졌다. 이것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들에게 경고하신 그대로였다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 이런 일이 일어날 것이라고 맹세하며 말씀하셨다. 그래서 백성은 몹시 고통을 받았다.

pt.L: Por onde quer que saíssem, a mão {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} estava contra eles para o mal, como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha falado e como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} lhes tinha jurado; e ficaram em grande aflição.
pt.B: Toda vez que saíam para lutar, a mão {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} estava contra eles para lhes trazer desgraça, exatamente como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha avisado e lhes tinha jurado. Eles ficaram em grande aflição.
pt.R: Toda vez que Israel saía para a batalha, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} estava contra eles, e eles eram derrotados. Era exatamente o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha avisado que aconteceria. {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} tinha prometido com juramento que isso aconteceria. Por isso o povo sofreu terrivelmente.

decisions.choice: went out: went out to war
alternatives: in everything they set out to do
decisions.reason: "Going out" is the word for marching out to battle (Deuteronomy 28:7, 25), and verse 14 has just spoken of enemies and plunderers.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD ... for harm: God's power at work against them
decisions.reason: The LORD's "hand" is his power in action, which had once fought for Israel (Exodus 14:31; Joshua 4:24). The word for "harm" is the same as "evil" in verse 11: Israel did evil, and the LORD brought evil, that is, disaster, on them. It is trouble, not wrongdoing, on God's side.

decisions.choice: as the LORD had spoken and sworn: the warnings of the covenant
decisions.reason: God had warned of defeat and distress if Israel served other gods (Leviticus 26:14-39; Deuteronomy 28:15-68; Joshua 23:15-16). What happens is not chance but the word he had given.

decisions.choice: to fight / to battle
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "went out" means here, as m1 explains.

decisions.choice: and they were defeated
decisions.reason: Readable says what it meant for the LORD's hand to be against them in battle.

source.text: וַיָּ֥קֶם יְהוָ֖ה שֹֽׁפְטִ֑ים וַיּ֣וֹשִׁיע֔וּם מִיַּ֖ד שֹׁסֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And raised up YHWH judges, and they saved them from [the] hand of their plunderers.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} raised up judges, and they saved them from the hand of their plunderers.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} raised up judges, who rescued them from the power of those who plundered them.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them leaders called judges. These judges rescued the people from the raiders.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akainua waamuzi, nao wakawaokoa mkononi mwa wateka nyara wao.
sw.B: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliinua waamuzi, waliowaokoa kutoka mikononi mwa wale waliowateka nyara.
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwapa viongozi walioitwa waamuzi. Waamuzi hao waliwaokoa watu kutoka kwa wavamizi.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} levantó jueces, y los salvaron de la mano de sus saqueadores.
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} levantó jueces, que los libraron del poder de los que los saqueaban.
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les dio líderes llamados jueces. Estos jueces libraron al pueblo de los saqueadores.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} suscita des juges, et ils les sauvèrent de la main de leurs pillards.
fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} suscita des juges, qui les délivrèrent du pouvoir de ceux qui les pillaient.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur a donné des chefs qu’on appelle des juges. Ces juges ont délivré le peuple des pillards.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} dấy lên các quan xét, và họ giải cứu dân khỏi tay những kẻ cướp bóc mình.
vi.B: Rồi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} dấy lên các quan xét, là những người giải cứu dân khỏi tay những kẻ cướp bóc họ.
vi.R: Rồi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban cho họ những thủ lĩnh gọi là quan xét. Những thủ lĩnh này giải cứu dân chúng khỏi những kẻ cướp.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 사사들을 일으키셨고, 그들이 그들을 약탈자들의 손에서 구원하였다.
ko.B: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 사사들을 세우셨고, 사사들은 그들을 약탈하는 자들의 손에서 구해 내었다.
ko.R: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 사사라고 불리는 지도자들을 그들에게 주셨다. 이 사사들은 약탈자들에게서 백성을 구해 내었다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} levantou juízes, e eles os salvaram da mão dos seus saqueadores.
pt.B: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} levantou juízes, que os livraram do poder daqueles que os saqueavam.
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} deu a eles líderes chamados juízes. Esses juízes livraram o povo dos saqueadores.

decisions.choice: judges: leaders the LORD raised up to rescue Israel and govern it
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to judge, to decide what is right, and so to rule. The judges of this book are more than court judges: they are leaders called by God for a crisis, who rescue Israel from its enemies in battle and then lead the people, as Othniel, Ehud, Deborah, Gideon and others do (3:9-11; 4:4-5). Some are not described as deciding cases at all. The same word is used for rulers in nearby languages of the time.

decisions.choice: the LORD raised up: the rescue is God's doing
decisions.reason: The judges do not rise by their own ambition or by Israel's choice. The LORD raises them up (3:9, 15) and is with them (verse 18). Here no repentance by Israel is mentioned; the rescue comes from his pity (verse 18).

decisions.choice: saved them: rescued them from their enemies
decisions.reason: The verb is the common word for saving; here, as through Judges, it is rescue from enemies in war (3:9, 31; 6:14).

decisions.choice: leaders called judges
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "judges" and adds "leaders" so a new reader does not picture judges in a court; where the verb "judged Israel" comes, Readable says "led Israel".

decisions.choice: rescued
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "rescued" for the rescue in battle that m3 describes; Literal keeps "saved".

decisions.choice: "mwamuzi, waamuzi" at every level; Readable "viongozi walioitwa waamuzi" here, and "aliwaongoza Israeli" for the verb
decisions.reason: The terms note sets "mwamuzi" for the title, the word Swahili readers know for these leaders (Acts 13:20 already says "waamuzi"). Like the English, Readable says once that they were leaders, since a "mwamuzi" today is a court judge or a referee, and later says "aliwaongoza Israeli" (led Israel) for the verb.

decisions.choice: "jueces" at every level ("líderes llamados jueces" at R); the verb "juzgar a Israel" (L, B), "dirigir a Israel" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Judges, as the terms note for these books sets: these were leaders the LORD raised up to rescue Israel and to govern it, more than judges in a court (m1). Spanish keeps "jueces", the name of the book, and Readable says what they were, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "des juges" at every level; Readable "des chefs qu'on appelle des juges"
decisions.reason: For Judges 1-10, as the terms note sets: the judges were leaders the LORD raised up to rescue Israel and govern it, more than judges in a court, as the meaning decision says. French keeps the traditional word that gives the book its name ("juge"; "il jugea Israël" at Literal and Balanced, "il dirigea Israël" at Readable), and Readable says they were leaders, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "quan xét" (L, B); "thủ lĩnh" (R), introduced as "những thủ lĩnh gọi là quan xét"
decisions.reason: These were leaders the LORD raised up to rescue Israel and govern it, more than court judges (m1). "quan xét" is the word of the Vietnamese Acts 13:20 and of the book's familiar name; Readable calls them "thủ lĩnh" (leaders), as the English Readable says "leaders", and the verb is "xét xử" (L, B) and "lãnh đạo" (R) wherever a judge governs Israel.

decisions.choice: "사사" for *shofet* at every level, with Readable adding that the judges were leaders
decisions.reason: "사사" is the word Korean readers know for these leaders, and Acts 13:20 in this translation already uses it. As the meaning decision says, they were leaders who rescued and governed Israel, more than court judges, so Readable calls them "사사라고 불리는 지도자들", as Acts 13:20 does at Readable.

decisions.choice: juízes (every level), líderes chamados juízes (R); julgar Israel (L, B), liderar Israel (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book. "Juiz" is the Portuguese word for the title, and the name of the book ("Juízes"); the leaders were more than court judges (m1), so Readable adds "líderes" here, as the English adds "leaders". Where the verb comes ("he judged Israel", 3:10; 4:4; 10:2-3; 12:7-14; 15:20; 16:31), Literal and Balanced say "julgou Israel" and Readable "liderou Israel", as the English Readable says "led Israel".

decisions.choice: salvaram (L); livraram (B, R); um libertador (3:9, 15)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the rescue in battle (m3) is "salvar" at Literal and "livrar" at Balanced and Readable, as the English says "saved" and "rescued". The noun from the same verb, used of Othniel and Ehud (3:9, 15), is "libertador".

source.text: וְגַ֤ם אֶל־שֹֽׁפְטֵיהֶם֙ לֹ֣א שָׁמֵ֔עוּ כִּ֣י זָנ֗וּ אַֽחֲרֵי֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם סָ֣רוּ מַהֵ֗ר מִן־הַדֶּ֜רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָלְכ֧וּ אֲבוֹתָ֛ם לִשְׁמֹ֥עַ מִצְוֺת־יְהוָ֖ה לֹא־עָ֥שׂוּ כֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And also to their judges not they listened, for they prostituted themselves after other gods and bowed down to them; they turned aside quickly from the way which walked their fathers, to obey [the] commandments of YHWH; not they did so.

en.L: And yet they did not listen even to their judges, for they prostituted themselves after other gods and bowed down to them. They turned aside quickly from the way in which their fathers had walked, obeying the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; they did not do so.
en.B: Yet they would not listen even to their judges. They gave themselves like prostitutes to other gods and bowed down to them. They were quick to turn from the path their {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} had walked, the path of obeying the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; they did not do as their {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} had done.
en.R: But the people would not even listen to their judges. They were not faithful to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Like a wife who leaves her husband for other men, they went after other gods and worshiped them. Their {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} had obeyed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s commands, but they quickly turned away from the way their {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} had lived. They did not obey as their {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} had.

sw.L: Lakini hata waamuzi wao hawakuwasikiliza, kwa maana walizini kwa kuifuata miungu mingine, wakaisujudia. Waligeuka upesi kutoka katika njia ambayo baba zao waliiendea, wakizitii amri za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; wao hawakufanya hivyo.
sw.B: Hata hivyo hawakuwasikiliza hata waamuzi wao. Walijitoa kama makahaba kwa miungu mingine, wakaisujudia. Waliiacha upesi njia ambayo mababu zao waliifuata, njia ya kuzitii amri za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; hawakufanya kama mababu zao walivyofanya.
sw.R: Lakini watu hawakuwasikiliza hata waamuzi wao. Hawakuwa waaminifu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Kama mke anayemwacha mume wake ili aende na wanaume wengine, waliifuata miungu mingine, wakaiabudu. Mababu zao walikuwa wametii amri za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, lakini wao waliiacha upesi njia ambayo mababu zao waliishi. Hawakutii kama mababu zao walivyotii.

es.L: Y tampoco a sus jueces escucharon, sino que se prostituyeron tras otros dioses y se postraron ante ellos. Se apartaron pronto del camino por el que habían andado sus padres, obedeciendo los mandamientos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; ellos no hicieron así.
es.B: Pero ni siquiera a sus jueces querían escuchar. Se entregaron como prostitutas a otros dioses y se postraron ante ellos. Pronto se apartaron del camino que habían seguido sus antepasados, el camino de obedecer los mandamientos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; no hicieron como sus antepasados.
es.R: Pero el pueblo ni siquiera escuchaba a sus jueces. No fueron fieles {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
